title: Files
description: M4: the file manager and file transfers between panel and agent. Every path is relative to the server's data folder (`/data` in the container) and resolved beneath it with `os.Root` (Go's openat-based confinement): `..`, absolute paths and symlinks that lead out are refused. Bytes travel base64-encoded, so every frame stays below `MAX_FRAME_BYTES`. Transfers are pulled by the panel: one request per chunk, at most `TRANSFER_WINDOW` in flight, which is the backpressure.

FILE_TEXT_MAX_BYTES.description: Largest file `files.read` returns and `files.write` accepts (the panel's text editor). Larger files are downloaded and uploaded instead.

FILES_LIST_MAX_ENTRIES.description: Most entries one `files.list` answer holds; `truncated` says more exist.

TRANSFER_CHUNK_BYTES.description: Largest chunk of one `transfer.read` answer or `transfer.write` request, in raw bytes (about 683 KiB as base64).

TRANSFER_WINDOW.description: Most `transfer.read` / `transfer.write` requests the panel keeps in flight per transfer.

TRANSFER_IDLE_SEC.description: The agent closes a transfer that saw no request for this long (an unfinished upload's temporary file is removed). Also every transfer is closed when the panel connection is replaced.

TRANSFER_MAX_OPEN.description: Most open transfers per agent; `transfer.open` beyond it answers `conflict`.

UPLOAD_DISK_RESERVE_BYTES.description: Free space an upload (or a write) must leave on the host's data disk; otherwise `no_space`.

UPLOAD_TEMP_DIR.description: Folder below the data folder where uploads are written before `transfer.commit` renames them into place (same filesystem, inside the same root). Emptied by the agent at startup.

x-messages.description: List one folder (not recursive), folders first, then by name.
One entry. A symlink is reported as itself (`symlink`, with `linkTarget`).
A whole regular file of at most `FILE_TEXT_MAX_BYTES` (`too_large` otherwise). `binary` is set (and no content sent) when it isn't UTF-8 text or holds a NUL byte.

Replace (or create) a regular file atomically: temporary file in the same folder, then rename. Keeps an existing file's mode; new files are 0644 and owned by GAME_UID. `conflict` when `expectedModifiedAt` is set and differs.
Create one folder (0755, GAME_UID); the parent must exist. `conflict` when the name is taken.
Rename or move within the data folder. `conflict` when the target exists and `overwrite` is false, or when a folder would move into itself.
Delete files and folders (folders recursively). A symlink is removed, never its target. The data folder itself can't be deleted.
Start a download (a regular file in the data folder, or a finished backup archive) or an upload (into `UPLOAD_TEMP_DIR`, checked against free disk and the server's disk limit first).
One chunk of a download, by offset (random access, so several may be in flight).
One chunk of an upload, by offset. Chunks may arrive out of order; ranges must not overlap or pass the announced size.
Finish an upload: check that the written ranges cover exactly [0, size), fsync, rename into place (honouring `overwrite`), hand it to GAME_UID, close the transfer.
Abort or finish a transfer: close the file; an uncommitted upload's temporary file is removed. Unknown ids are not an error.

FileType.description: other = sockets, devices, fifos: listed, never opened.

path.description: Relative to the data folder, `/`-separated, no leading slash; `""` is the data folder itself.

modifiedAt.description: RFC 3339 with nanoseconds, UTC. Pass it back unchanged as `expectedModifiedAt`.

linkTarget.description: symlink only: where it points, as stored (it may lead out of the data folder; following it is refused then).

path.description: Relative to the data folder; `""` = the data folder.

truncated.description: More than `FILES_LIST_MAX_ENTRIES` entries exist; only the first ones (in order) are listed.

binary.description: Not UTF-8 text (or holds a NUL byte): `contentBase64` is empty.

expectedModifiedAt.description: The `modifiedAt` the editor loaded; a different current value answers `conflict`. null = create or overwrite without checking.

to.description: Full new path (a move when the folder differs). The parent must exist.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at `to` (never a folder).

TransferSource.description: file: a path in the data folder; backup: a finished backup archive (download only).

path.description: source file: the file to download, or the upload's final path (its folder must exist).

backupId.description: source backup: the panel's backup id.

size.description: upload: exact byte count (the browser's Content-Length).

overwrite.description: upload: replace an existing file at `path` on commit.

name.description: Base name of the file (`<backupId>.tar.zst` for a backup; the panel names that download after the server and the backup itself).

size.description: download: bytes to read (the panel sends it as Content-Length); upload: the announced size.

dataBase64.description: Shorter than asked only at the end of the file.

eof.description: offset + length reached the size from `transfer.open`.
